name: Mecobalamin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Mecobalamin (methylcobalamin) is an active vitamin B12 form, cleared mainly by the kidneys. The Japanese tablet insert does not address kidney impairment; a 2024 Japanese regulatory review of high-dose injection found only modest exposure increases with kidney impairment and concluded no dose adjustment is needed, with limited data in severe impairment. It has no US FDA drug label.
kidney_function_basis: Japanese sources describe kidney impairment as mild, moderate or severe without dose changes; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual oral dose: 1,500 micrograms/day in 3 divided doses (500 micrograms three times daily); reassess if no effect after several months (PMDA insert).

No dose adjustment: a Japanese regulatory review of high-dose intramuscular mecobalamin (50 mg twice weekly) found exposure rises modestly with kidney impairment (AUC about 1.2-fold mild, 1.6-fold moderate) and concluded no adjustment is needed, including severe impairment (limited data). The oral tablet insert does not address kidney function.

monitoring: Clinical response in peripheral neuropathy; do not continue for months without benefit (PMDA insert).
